summary:
Radar for 1 Nov 2026 (GLP-1 focus). There's no qualifying Lane C news today. I checked the big headlines and none of them is a new randomized result from the last 48 hours:
- The Mounjaro heart-risk approval is from 28 Aug 2026; the Nov 1 stories are re-covering it.
- The EU approval of the Wegovy pill is from 16 Jul 2026.
- The ABC "heat wave" GLP-1 warning is a July story being re-shared.
- The retatrutide sleep apnea trials were published in NEJM on 21 Oct.
- The retatrutide vs Ozempic trial (TRANSCEND-T2D-2) came out on 28 Oct and is already everywhere.
- Lilly's Q3 report (29 Oct) only says EloraTZP moves to Phase 3 in Q4. That's status news, so it's a Short.

So the long-form slots go to Lane A, ranked by momentum and how far the topic has climbed across our snapshots:
1. Stopping tirzepatide. Seen 7 times, momentum up to 86. New hooks: grocers getting ready for shoppers who come off GLP-1s (Food Dive, Oct 30) and the semaglutide persistence study (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 29).
2. Hair loss. Seen 8 times and still climbing.
3. Fatigue and tiredness. This is the next topic on the playbook's list, and a GLP-1 fatigue article ran on Oct 30.
4. Thanksgiving on tirzepatide. Seasonal, with search interest likely to peak 18–27 Nov.
5. A breakfast question, hooked to EatingWell's Nov 1 piece. It's a new question for the Lane A cluster.

The best emerging Short is the 30 Oct JAMA piece on whether GLP-1 medicines are safe for people with frailty. It covers semaglutide's SELECT trial data across frailty levels, alongside an Oct 7 cohort study on frailty and falls. It fits the "honest uncertainty" body-worry format, but the evidence covers semaglutide and GLP-1s as a class, not tirzepatide, so tirzepatide can't go in the title.

Other good Shorts:
- Retatrutide sleep apnea, framed as "what's confirmed?"
- Retatrutide side effects and dropouts in TRANSCEND-T2D-2.
- Tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder risk (scoping review).
- Alcohol at holiday meals.
- What EloraTZP moving to Phase 3 actually means.

Rejected: the peptide liver-failure and "meds bought online" stories as hooks, the Forbes "where to buy" and Page Six "$99 start" affiliate pieces, and all cost or coverage news (open-enrollment cuts, Bloomberg's employer-coverage story).

Two items need care before use:
- The Psychiatric Times story on GLP-1s and eating disorders: only as a calm "talk to your prescriber" piece, never anything that could read as encouraging restriction.
- The ACOG pregnancy guidance plus the new meta-analysis.

Writers should check every number against the primary source. The fatigue rates especially must come from the current Zepbound and Mounjaro labels, not from blog summaries.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (783 began the lead-in, then 335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo), refreshed by the semaglutide persistence cohort (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 29) and 'grocers getting ready for post-GLP-1 shoppers' (Food Dive, Oct 30)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Open on a 'you' scenario and answer the question in the first 15 seconds. Explain why appetite and weight tend to come back (the hormone signal stops; nothing has 'failed'). Show what the people who stayed on treatment kept. Cover the habits the evidence supports for any future plan made with a prescriber: protein, strength training, regular routines. Say 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own' word for word. Calm and encouraging. Before-after thumbnail: 'When it stops'.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
do you gain weight back after tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: Steady now, with a bump in early January (New Year and insurance changes)
candidates.why_now: Seen in 7 snapshots with momentum rising from 76 to 86, and it's next on the playbook's Lane A list. Two new hooks this week: Food Dive (Oct 30) and South Florida Reporter (Nov 1) on grocers preparing for people coming off GLP-1s, plus the Oct 29 Diabetes Obes Metab persistence cohort. Open enrollment, with coverage shrinking, is pushing people to search what happens if they stop.

evidence.signal: Early treatment trajectory and long-term persistence with semaglutide, population cohort, Oct 29 2026
Are grocers ready to help shoppers getting off GLP-1s? (Oct 30)
Patterns of discontinuation, restarting and switching of semaglutide and tirzepatide in adults with obesity

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? 5.4% (119/2,183) vs 0.9% (22/2,221) (Gupta 2026); the label reports 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men. Refreshed by the new Cureus meta-analysis of skin side effects in semaglutide randomized trials and the Med Sci (Basel) review
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (the L1 10-30 redo). Open with the shower-drain moment and the honest answer: it's uncommon, it's particularly associated with rapid weight loss, and it's usually temporary shedding. Explain telogen effluvium simply. Cover what helps: enough protein, iron and nutrient checks with a clinician, patience. Say 'no human studies show a direct effect on follicles'. Never say 'it isn't the drug'.
keywords: hair loss on GLP-1 how to stop
candidates.why_now: Seen in 8 snapshots with momentum still edging up (72→77). A new randomized-trial meta-analysis of semaglutide skin side effects (Cureus) adds a fresh hook. Our hair-loss Shorts got 106 views on YouTube and 142 on Instagram, and the long-form redo is still pending.

evidence.signal: Cutaneous adverse events with semaglutide: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
Skin side effects with semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide: systematic review (Oct 9)

candidates.topic: Why am I so tired on tirzepatide? Fatigue rates in the label vs placebo, plus the likely everyday drivers (eating much less, too little fluid, nausea), and what helps
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Title: 'Tirzepatide Fatigue: Why You're Tired and What Helps'. Open with the 3 pm crash and the quick answer: fatigue is a listed, usually mild side effect. Then cover the everyday factors you can change: enough protein and total food, fluids (thirst can drop), sleep, steady movement. Explain when to call a prescriber: dizziness, signs of low blood sugar if you take insulin or sulfonylureas, ongoing vomiting. Use 'may' and 'can'. No dosing talk.
keywords: why am I so tired on Zepbound
candidates.predicted_peak: Steady, ongoing demand; refreshed this week
candidates.why_now: Next on the playbook's priority list (fatigue and hydration). Yahoo ran 'GLP-1s and Fatigue: Why You Feel Tired' on Oct 30, and 'tired on tirzepatide' is a common user question. Shorter days and the clock change on Nov 1 add a seasonal 'I'm exhausted' hook. Take fatigue percentages from the current Zepbound and Mounjaro labels only; third-party blogs differ.

evidence.signal: GLP-1s and Fatigue: Why You Feel Tired and How to Bounce Back (Oct 30)

evidence.source: Web / Ro (secondary, for context only; verify against the label)
evidence.signal: Does tirzepatide make you tired? A common consumer search question

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller plates, eating slower, alcohol and easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, published around Nov 10–18 so suggested traffic builds before the 26th. Open with 'you're at the table, three bites in, and you're full': why that happens (slower stomach emptying), then a plate plan, pacing, which rich foods are more likely to bring on nausea, and drinks. Support the long-form with 2–3 Shorts. No 'avoid the feast' or extreme-restriction messaging; enjoying the meal is the goal.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots across two variants, holding at 76–78. A seasonal cycle is about to start. Our Halloween food-noise Short got 87 views by day 2, which shows timely life-on-the-drug hooks work. Long-form needs about a week to pick up suggested traffic, so publish by mid-November.

evidence.signal: Dietitians' GLP-1 meal guidance is circulating (Nov 1)
How digital food-purchase patterns respond to GLP-1-based treatment (Oct 29); context for how food choices shift

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines after 65 and frailty: JAMA (Oct 30) on SELECT's semaglutide heart results across frailty levels, plus the Diabetes Obes Metab cohort (Oct 7) linking GLP-1 starts with slightly less frailty progression and fewer falls than DPP-4 inhibitors
candidates.angle: 08:00 'honest uncertainty' body-worry Short. Frame it as reassurance with limits. The heart benefit in SELECT held across frailty levels (adults with heart disease and overweight or obesity, without diabetes). The observational cohort is 'linked to' slightly fewer falls. But neither shows the medicine preserves strength, which is why protein and strength training matter. Title the drug class or semaglutide, not tirzepatide; the data doesn't cover tirzepatide.
candidates.why_now: The JAMA piece went up Oct 30 and only a few consumer outlets have picked it up so far (WorldHealth.net, Oct 31). Few creator videos on it yet. Our bones Short (241 views) shows body-worry Shorts about ageing do well. It's also a natural lead-in to our strength-training long-form.

evidence.signal: Analysis Asks: Are GLP-1 Drugs Safe in People With Frailty? (Oct 30)
GLP-1 RA use linked to slightly less frailty progression and fewer falls vs DPP-4 inhibitors (observational)
Do GLP-1 Drugs Raise Your Risk of Falling After 65? (Oct 31)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide for breakfast: what to eat in the morning when you're not hungry (protein-forward, gentle on nausea), hooked to EatingWell's 'the #1 breakfast dietitians recommend on a GLP-1' (Nov 1)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, or a second Lane A slot. Answer a narrow question people type: 'What should I eat for breakfast on tirzepatide?' Cover why skipping can backfire for protein and energy, easy higher-protein options, small portions, and fluids. Present these as our own tips, without source tags. Link it into the 'Life on Tirzepatide' playlist next to Protein and What to Eat. It must answer a different question from What to Eat.
keywords: what to eat for breakfast on Zepbound
not hungry in the morning Mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–2 weeks after the EatingWell syndication spreads, then steady
candidates.why_now: EatingWell published Nov 1 and gets wide syndication (MSN, Yahoo). Protein on Tirzepatide had our fastest Lane A start (87 views at day 2, 14.3% CTR). A tight long-tail meal question feeds the suggested-video cluster that drives about 70% of Lane A minutes.

evidence.signal: The #1 Breakfast Dietitians Recommend If You're on a GLP-1 Medication (Nov 1)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and sleep apnea: what's confirmed. TRIUMPH-1-OSA (243 adults without type 2 diabetes) and TRIUMPH-2-OSA (448 with type 2 diabetes), NEJM Oct 21. In the no-diabetes trial, breathing interruptions (AHI) fell by 34.3 (9 mg) and 31.7 (12 mg) events per hour vs 9.9 on placebo at 80 weeks
candidates.angle: 13:00 retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending. Give the result, state it's still investigational and not approved (Lilly plans an FDA filing in Q1 2027), and note that tirzepatide is already approved for sleep apnea in adults with obesity, as a recognition anchor. Both trials enrolled BMI 27 or higher. Don't compare across trials as if head-to-head.
keywords: new weight loss drug sleep apnea
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–7 days (consumer pickup is still spreading: Medical News Today Oct 30, Gizmodo)
candidates.why_now: Phase 3 results were published in NEJM and presented at the European Sleep Research Society. The consumer wave is building (Medical News Today Oct 30, AOL syndication). Retatrutide Shorts built on Phase 3 data hit 270, 205 and 122 views. It's not a Lane C long-form, because it's more than 48 hours old.

evidence.signal: Investigational drug tied to substantial reduction in sleep apnea severity
Triple-action weekly drug reduces sleep apnea in two late-stage trials
Experimental weight-loss drug retatrutide may help improve sleep apnea (Oct 30)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder: what a new scoping review shows (11 RCTs; pancreatitis in 11 participants across 5 trials; gallstones in 73 trial participants) (Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes, Oct 23), plus the propensity-matched real-world comparison (J Clin Med, Oct 16)
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry Short, or a Lane A long-form ('Tirzepatide and Your Gallbladder: What to Know'). Explain why rapid weight loss is linked to gallstones, which symptoms mean you should call a clinician right away (severe upper-belly pain, pain spreading to the back, fever, yellowing skin), and keep the uncommon numbers in context. Say the counts in the source's own units. Calm mascot, no green checks.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 4 snapshots (62–74) with two fresh reviews in October. Our earlier gallbladder Short got only 56 views, so lead with tirzepatide in the title and use the new review numbers. It fits Lane A as a long-form question users actually type.

evidence.signal: Pancreatic and gallbladder adverse events with tirzepatide in obesity: scoping review (Oct 23)
Biliary and pancreatic safety: tirzepatide vs semaglutide vs DPP-4 inhibitors, propensity-matched (Oct 16)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs Ozempic in type 2 diabetes: the side-effect and dropout side of TRANSCEND-T2D-2 (Oct 28 topline; Medical Daily: 'more patients quit over side effects'), including the dysesthesia skin-sensation signal (4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%)
candidates.angle: 13:00 Short with a different angle from the headline efficacy story: 'the trade-off nobody headlined'. Cover side-effect discontinuation and dysesthesia, framed calmly as topline, not yet peer-reviewed. Keep it to 1 Short this week (one-trial cap). Population: adults with type 2 diabetes; comparator semaglutide 2 mg. Say 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'.
candidates.why_now: The efficacy headline is saturated (Medscape, CTV, EMJ, BioPharm, News18, Scripps), but the tolerability angle is thinly covered. Our dysesthesia Short got 54 views at day 1; recheck it before making another.

evidence.signal: Retatrutide beat Ozempic but more patients quit over side effects (Oct 30)
Lilly's triple-action drug beats Novo's Ozempic in Phase 3 trial
Lilly sets up next-gen obesity battle with full Phase 3 retatrutide data

candidates.topic: Alcohol on tirzepatide at holiday parties: why a drink may hit differently, and what research is exploring (Medscape clinician view Oct 28; PET-imaging tirzepatide alcohol use disorder trial protocol; Heineken's 'GLP-1 problem')
candidates.angle: Short now, and a Thanksgiving tie-in later. What's known: alcohol can worsen nausea and low blood sugar risk for people on certain diabetes medicines, and it adds calories when appetite is low. What's still research: whether GLP-1-type medicines reduce cravings (a trial protocol is not a result). No 'treats alcoholism' claims.
candidates.predicted_peak: Mid-November to late December (holiday drinking season)
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots across trade, clinical and business press. Holiday parties are the seasonal trigger, and searches for 'can I drink on Zepbound' will rise from mid-November.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide goes under the PET scanner in a new alcohol use disorder trial protocol (Oct 29)
Roadmap for GLP-1 receptor agonists in substance use disorders (Oct 30)

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) heads to Phase 3 in Q4 2026 (Lilly Q3 report, Oct 29), with Phase 2 showing greater weight loss and A1C reduction vs tirzepatide 15 mg in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Short pointing to the live EloraTZP long-form (our only proven Lane C spike). One fact: what moving to Phase 3 means and what's still unknown. Status news only, so it's a Short, not a long-form. End: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.'
candidates.predicted_peak: When the Phase 3 start is announced (Q4 2026)
candidates.why_now: Lilly confirmed the Phase 3 start in its Oct 29 Q3 report (Morningstar: 'another high-efficacy medicine advancing to Phase 3'). It's a ready-made funnel to a long-form that already earns subscribers.

evidence.signal: EloraTZP Phase 2 results; Phase 3 to begin Q4 2026
Lilly amylin + tirzepatide combo boosts weight loss in trial (Sep 30)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your heart in type 2 diabetes: what the new label claim actually says (SURPASS-CVOT, about 13,300 adults with type 2 diabetes and heart or blood-vessel disease; 8% lower relative risk of major cardiovascular events vs dulaglutide over about 4 years; FDA indication Aug 28 2026)
candidates.angle: Calm 'what's confirmed?' Short for people with type 2 diabetes. It showed non-inferiority to dulaglutide, the 8% figure is relative and needs an absolute rate next to it, and it applies only to the SURPASS-CVOT population. Not a long-form (single-trial deep dives on approved drugs are banned).
candidates.why_now: Re-coverage on Nov 1 (scanx) and Oct 30 (GreaterGood) is bringing the August approval back into feeds. Low urgency; only worth it as a precise, population-correct fact Short.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide gets FDA approval to cut cardiovascular risk in type 2 diabetes
FDA approves Mounjaro to help lower heart attack and stroke risk in adults with type 2 diabetes

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and pregnancy planning: ACOG's October 2026 guidance plus a new time-window-stratified meta-analysis of pregnancy outcomes after exposure to GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 medicines (Front Pharmacol, Oct 16)
candidates.angle: Calm Short for people who might become pregnant. ACOG suggests considering stopping 1–2 months before trying to conceive, as a decision with your clinician. Explain what the meta-analysis can and can't tell us (observational exposure data). Quote ACOG only for what it actually says (an earlier Short was held for misattributing ACOG). No personal stop instructions; always 'plan this with your prescriber or OB'.
candidates.why_now: A new meta-analysis plus the October ACOG guidance (seen in a snapshot at momentum 78). Strong search intent among women 25–40.

evidence.signal: Pregnancy and perinatal outcomes after GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP exposure: meta-analysis (Oct 16)

candidates.topic: Why do GLP-1 medicines work? Scientists still debate the mechanism (The Observer, Oct 30): gut signals vs brain reward, gastric emptying, and 'food noise'
candidates.angle: How-it-works Short, or a Lane A segment: 'Tirzepatide and Food Noise: What's Happening in Your Brain'. Show what's established (GLP-1 receptors in the brain's appetite centres, slower stomach emptying) and what's still open (how much each contributes, and the GIP part of tirzepatide). Positive and curious. Don't title it as a broad head term.
candidates.why_now: Mainstream UK pickup (The Observer, Oct 30) plus the Metabolism review on the metabolic-brain axis (Oct 30). It refreshes the evergreen how-it-works pillar.

evidence.signal: Weight-loss drugs work, but scientists still don't agree on why (Oct 30)
The metabolic-brain axis: GLP-1 signalling and obesity pharmacotherapy (Oct 30)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and eating disorders: Psychiatric Times (Oct 30) on how GLP-1s may reinforce restriction in people with eating disorders
candidates.angle: Only as a compassionate 'who should talk to their prescriber first' Short. Encourage disclosure of any eating-disorder history and point to support lines (spoken and on screen). No eating-less framing, no numbers that could read as targets. Needs Editor-in-Chief sign-off; skip if it can't be done gently.
candidates.why_now: Fresh clinical commentary. A real safety question, but high-risk for the brand's eating-disorder guardrail.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists May Reinforce Restriction in Patients With Eating Disorders (Oct 30)

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'I injected a peptide to lose weight and my liver started failing' (NY Post, Oct 30), 'weight loss meds bought online' hospitalisation (LSM, Oct 30), 'Stars use GLP-1s, start for just $99' (Page Six), 'Best online tirzepatide programs / where to buy' (Forbes), and GLP-1 cost and coverage stories
candidates.angle: Don't make content from these. They're sourcing, affiliate or cost angles, or single-case scare stories. If a dated FDA or MHRA warning about research-chemical peptides comes out, it can feed the once-a-week gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Short, which never names sellers or how to buy.
candidates.why_now: High news volume, but it breaks the channel's rules on gray-market sources, cost topics and scare framing.

evidence.signal: Peptide injection and liver failure, a single first-person account (Oct 30)
